H1.whisper_text: On the night of the 8th of December 1980, John Lennon came home to the Dakota, the apartment building on Central Park West in New York.

H2.whisper_text: He was 40 years old and he was shot a few steps from his own front door.

H3.whisper_text: This is what the record shows about his last day, and about the days after.

1.1.whisper_text: John Lennon was born in Liverpool on the 9th of October, 1940.

1.2.whisper_text: The Beatles broke up in 1970, and in 1971 he moved to New York with Yoko Ono.

1.3.whisper_text: By 1973, they were living at the Dakota, a 19th century building that faces Central Park.

1.4.whisper_text: On the 9th of October 1975, his 35th birthday, their son Sean was born.

1.5.whisper_text: After that, Lennon stepped away from the music business for about five years and stayed home to raise his son.

1.6.whisper_text: In June 1980, he took Shawn to Bermuda, and there the songs began to come.

1.8.whisper_text: From August to October they recorded at the Hit Factory, a studio in New York.

1.8b.whisper_text: In September, they signed with Geffen Records.

1.9.whisper_text: The album, Double Fantasy, came out on the 17th of November 1980, and it was his first in more than five years.

2.1.whisper_text: On Saturday, the 6th of December, he gave a long interview to Andy Peebles of BBC Radio 1.

2.1b.whisper_text: Double Fantasy had been in the shops for three weeks.

2.2.whisper_text: Two days later, Monday, the 8th of December, was another working day at the Dakota.

2.3.whisper_text: In the afternoon, the photographer Annie Leibovites took pictures of Lenin and Ono in their apartment, and she left at half -past three.

2.4.whisper_text: Then, a crew from RKO radio arrived, and Lennon gave what would be his last interview.

2.5.whisper_text: Around five o 'clock the couple left for the record plant a recording studio to work on a song of Ono's called walking on thin ice

2.6.whisper_text: At the door, a man who had been waiting asked Lennon to sign a copy of Double Fantasy.

2.7.whisper_text: Lennon signed it and they drove away

2.8.whisper_text: They worked in the studio into the late evening, and at about 10 .50 they came back to the Dakota.

2.9.whisper_text: Lennon planned to say goodnight to his son.

2.10.whisper_text: As they walked in through the archway, the man who had asked for the autograph was still there.

2.11.whisper_text: He fired at Lennon from a few feet away.

2.12.whisper_text: Police officers arrived about two minutes later and arrested the gunman on the spot.

2.13.whisper_text: Two officers drove Lennon to Roosevelt Hospital in their patrol car.

2.14.whisper_text: His death certificate gives the time of death as 1115, though another time has also been reported.

3.1.whisper_text: That night, Monday night football was on American television.

3.2.whisper_text: During the game, Howard Cosell told the viewers that Lennon was dead on arrival and then the game went on.

3.3.whisper_text: Outside the Dakota, people began to gather that night and they kept coming all night.

3.4.whisper_text: The next day, Yoko Ono said that there would be no funeral.

3.5.whisper_text: Her statement ended, John loved and prayed for the human race. Please pray the same for him.

3.6.whisper_text: Paul McCartney, speaking to reporters outside his home in Sussex, said, I can't take it at the moment.

3.7.whisper_text: George Harrison said in a statement, after all we went through together, I had and still have great love and respect for him.

3.8.whisper_text: Ringo Starr, who was in the Bahamas, flew to New York to console Ono and Shawn.

3.9.whisper_text: Lennon was cremated on the 9th of December at Ferncliffe Cemetery and his ashes were scattered in Central Park.

3.10.whisper_text: Instead of a funeral, Oh No! asked for 10 minutes of silence on Sunday, the 14th of December.

3.11.whisper_text: In Central Park, estimates of the crowd run from 50 ,000 to more than 100 ,000.

3.12.whisper_text: In Liverpool, reports of the crowd run from 15 ,000 to 30 ,000.

3.13.whisper_text: Radio stations in New York went off the air for those 10 minutes.

3.14.whisper_text: In San Diego, people gathered in Balboa Park.

3.15.whisper_text: and at a record store there, Double Fantasy had sold out the day after his death.

3.16.whisper_text: It had been on sale at $5 .99, and when it was restocked, the price was $6 .99.

4.1.whisper_text: The gunman pleaded guilty to second -degree murder against his lawyer's advice to plead insanity.

4.2.whisper_text: In 1981, he was sentenced to 20 years to life.

4.3.whisper_text: He became eligible for parole in the year 2000 and has been denied it at least 14 times.

4.4.whisper_text: At the next Grammy Awards, Double Fantasy won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

4.5.whisper_text: On the 9th of October 1985, what would have been Lennon's 45th birthday, New York, dedicated a memorial in Central Park across from the Dakota?

4.6.whisper_text: It is called Strawberry Fields. Bono and the Mayor, Ed Koch, dedicated it, and Ono gave more than a million dollars toward its upkeep.

4.7.whisper_text: Every year, on the 8th of December, fans gather there.

Z1.whisper_text: He had been back at work for only a few months.

Z2.whisper_text: What would he have made next?
